set.approach: Park at the pullout used for the Wall of the '90s in Clear Creek Canyon, then follow the creek south toward the Punk Rock wall and the crags beyond it. Cross to the west bank on the frozen creek, or by the Tyrolean traverse if the creek is open, and keep going south on that side. A short scree gully climbs to the M3 Crag, a winter-oriented wall just west of the second tunnel, behind the Mission Wall.
set.descent_text: Parties lower or rappel from the fixed slings at the top, or walk off to climber's left (southwest).

review.notes: Area page gives parking, creek crossing, scree gully and the descent options; the M2 page confirms the crag's loose rock. Area-level descent applied to each line; one source.

set.approach: Start at the McCullough Gulch trailhead and hike the road, staying on it past the private mining claims. Keep on the road until it narrows to a trail, then drop through brush to the beaver ponds and skirt them on their west side. From there a scree and talus slope leads east, angling up toward the base of the climb. Check the avalanche forecast, since the gulch has avalanche terrain.
set.descent_text: Traverse east from the top and walk down the prominent boxed couloir. Avalanche conditions in that couloir deserve attention, so check the forecast.

review.notes: Claim Jumper page gives the road, claims, beaver ponds, talus and the east traverse into the boxed couloir; Blue Gold page places that route in the couloir beside it.

set.approach: Use the approach for the neighboring Claim Jumper: the McCullough Gulch trailhead, the road past the private mining claims, then the beaver ponds and the talus slope beyond. Blue Gold is on the steep face partway up the couloir, left of Claim Jumper. Check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Walk off to the left and go down the couloir. Some seasons leave a short ice step in the couloir, which is bypassed with a V-thread rappel back to the base.

review.notes: Blue Gold page gives its position and the descent; Claim Jumper page gives the shared approach. Single source for the descent.

set.approach: Follow the Claim Jumper approach from the McCullough Gulch trailhead to the beaver ponds, then hike west toward the large terminal moraine of the rock glacier. The line is on the north side of Quandary Peak. In winter the gulch road is closed by snow, which adds distance but little gain. Check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Noxious Fumes and Canary Couloir pages agree on the approach via the beaver ponds and moraine, and on the east ridge descent.

set.approach: Follow the Claim Jumper approach from the McCullough Gulch trailhead to the beaver ponds, then hike west toward the large terminal moraine of the rock glacier. The route is the striking couloir weakness in the north face of Quandary Peak. Early sun on the couloir's east-facing wall sends rocks down, so a hard overnight freeze and an early start help. Check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: The east ridge is the top-out, and the standard east ridge route leads back down. A third-class escape gully on climber's left about halfway up may reach the east ridge sooner.

review.notes: Canary Couloir page gives the couloir, rockfall note, escape gully and east ridge descent; Noxious Fumes page agrees on approach and descent.

set.approach: Reach the same area as the Canary Couloir by the McCullough Gulch approach (trailhead, beaver ponds, then west toward the moraine), or cut across from the foot of the Inwood Arete. The line is on the east face that forms the Inwood Arete. Check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Descend the east ridge or the Quandary Couloir.

review.notes: Sluice Box page gives its location relative to the Canary Couloir and the descent; Canary page gives the approach.

set.approach: Drive to the upper Blue Lake dam on the Blue Lakes road and walk to the slab, a small south-facing patch of rock and ice just uphill and north of Lower Blue Lake. A large gully to its west holds avalanche potential, so check the avalanche forecast. The line is a thin band of ice and rock in the middle of the slab.

review.notes: Area page gives access and the gully; route page gives its place on the slab.

set.approach: Drive to the upper Blue Lake dam on the Blue Lakes road and walk to the slab, a small south-facing patch of rock and ice just uphill and north of Lower Blue Lake. A large gully to its west holds avalanche potential, so check the avalanche forecast. This is the largest stretch of ice visible from the road, on the east side of the slab; thick ice near the top takes screw anchors.

review.notes: Area page gives access; route page says it is the biggest ice visible from the road.

set.approach: Drive to the upper Blue Lake dam on the Blue Lakes road and walk to the slab, a small south-facing patch of rock and ice just uphill and north of Lower Blue Lake. review.notes: Area page gives access; route page places it at the west end.

set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge Trailhead and, after the second bridge, take the winter trail past Mills Lake and Jewel Lake to Black Lake (or reach it by way of Solitude Lake), then climb an easier iced section toward McHenry's Peak. The couloir system is on the northeast face; begin at the short slab that forms a weakness in the lowest rock band.

review.notes: Area page gives the Glacier Gorge approach; route page gives the start.

The route follows the right-hand flank of the big buttress on the east face.

review.notes: Area page gives the approach; route page places the route on the buttress.

set.approach: Use the Grays and Torreys approach to the parking lot at the end of the Stevens Gulch road. The road up from Bakerville is usually not drivable in winter, so plan to ski, snowshoe or walk it. McClellan's west face rises steeply east of the lot, and the couloir is the obvious line up it, with the ice step low down.
set.descent_text: Walk off down the prominent drainage on climber's right (south) of the route.

review.notes: Route page gives the line and descent drainage; area page gives the winter road approach.

set.approach: From the signed Maggie Gulch junction past Middleton, follow the gulch road (CR 23) up to a fork. The falls should be in view on the right. Work over to the creek at the fork, or follow the old road bed a little farther, to reach the ice. The road is usually snowed in by winter, and ice often forms before that. The creek holds debris from slides, so this is avalanche terrain; check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Rappel from a tree anchor set back from the top of the ice; double ropes may be needed. Or walk off left or right.

review.notes: Route page gives the fork, creek entry, avalanche note and descent; area page gives the junction and road.

set.approach: From the signed Maggie Gulch junction past Middleton, follow the gulch road (CR 23) up to a fork, then work over to the creek at the fork, or follow the old road bed a little farther. It is the lefthand one of a pair of falls in the creek that runs alongside the road, a short pillar left of the obvious waterfall; low-angle slabs lead to its base. Slide debris in the creek marks this as avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Debris can make rappelling tricky. The easiest way off is up the creek, which is snow or WI2 ice, and then up the steep bank on the left to the road.

review.notes: Route page gives location, avalanche note and descent; area page gives the junction.
